metadata.note: Asherton and Gulf Railway (Nueces Valley, Rio Grande and Mexico Ry until Mar 9 1909), Artesia Wells - Asherton, Texas, 32.5 mi. One feature, drawn 1916-1920 per the research report's drawable: field. Research report: research/branches/asherton_and_gulf_railway.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 split would fall at the Jan 2 1926 Missouri Pacific Lines purchase (via the NOT&M / Gulf Coast Lines; the A&G corporation survived until the Mar 1 1956 MP merger). It lies outside the drawable 1916-1920 span, so there is one feature in the A&G's own colour. #C04F7A is new; a script confirmed no other company in data/ uses it.
not_yet_sourced: asherton-gulf-artesia-wells-asherton: START [OPEN] at 1916 and END [OPEN] at 1920. Opening Jun 27 / Aug 2 1909 (ICC, TSHA) vs 'began running in 1910' (TSHA Asherton entry) vs a 1908 photo caption (Texas Escapes) - no source says passengers were carried from opening. No source dates the end of passenger service; the doodlebug was bought at an unknown date after 1920; the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 108 'Asherton & Gulf Railway' survives in OCR without times or a 'Freight Service only' line, so 1951 is neither confirmed nor denied. Whether passengers continued under MP Lines after Jan 1926 is unconfirmed. Best next sources: Railroad Commission of Texas annual reports, Moody's/Poor's manuals, Portal to Texas History newspapers (Carrizo Springs Javelin).
Geometry: the eastern ~10 mi (Artesia Wells - about MP 10.5) is a straight line; the actual grade there is unmapped in OSM and OHM.

properties.line: Asherton and Gulf: Artesia Wells – Asherton
properties.speed_source: Estimated. No A&G timetable with running times was found; 25 km/h is a guess for a daily mixed train (a coach on the freight) over 32.5 miles of rural short line with switching at the onion-shipping stations.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (overpass-api.de, 2026-11-20), routed with opstrace.py. No old_railway_operator tag for this road exists in the corridor (only MP on the UP Laredo Subdivision main line at Artesia Wells). The grade survives in OSM as railway=razed ways named 'Asherton & Gulf' (way 150258672, plus 150258668/150258670 in Asherton). OpenHistoricalMap has only the I-GN main line in the 28.24,-99.82 to 28.50,-99.24 box, no A&G way.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 31.7 mi against 32.489 mi documented (ICC valuation main line; Fowler mileposts Artesia Wells 0.0 - Asherton 32.0). 21.5 mi on the OSM railway=razed 'Asherton & Gulf' ways, from Asherton through Catarina to the point where the mapped grade stops at 28.3144 N, 99.4491 W (around Fowler MP 10-11, between Light MP 12.0 and Farmington MP 6.0). STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: that point - Artesia Wells junction on the UP/ex-I-GN main line, 10.3 mi, a ruled chord through Farmington, Happle and Bart; no OSM, OHM or rail-trail trace of this stretch exists, and FM 133 (which parallels it) runs about 1 km south of the mapped grade, so it was not used as a stand-in. Waypoints within 0.8 km (Artesia Wells 0.0, Catarina 0.8, Asherton 0.5 km; all three geocodes checked as the La Salle / Dimmit County places, not counties). The razed-way trace is a modern mapper's reconstruction of the lifted 1909 grade, not a surveyed alignment.

segments.note: Asherton and Gulf mixed-train passenger service, Artesia Wells (junction with the I-GN San Antonio - Laredo main line) - Catarina - Asherton. 1916 is confirmed by TSHA's figure of $5,000 passenger earnings that year and by Lula appearing in the 1916 Official Guide (Fowler); 1920 by the Texas Transportation Museum's figure of 7,645 passengers carried, all on mixed trains (a coach on the daily freight). BOTH ENDS ARE [OPEN]: these are the first and last CONFIRMED years, not known dates. The line opened Jun 27 / Aug 2 1909 and a gasoline railbus was bought some time after 1920, so service very likely ran on both sides, but no other year is confirmed. Missouri Pacific Lines bought the road Jan 2 1926 (via the NOT&M / Gulf Coast Lines); any post-1926 passenger years belong in a separate Missouri Pacific-coloured feature. The line was abandoned in 1958 - that is not a passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min (one mixed train each way daily) is an estimate from the 1920 'daily freight' description, not a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1916 from the TSHA Asherton and Gulf Railway entry (1916 passenger earnings) and Fowler's branchline.uk Texas station list (Lula tagged 1916G); 1920 and the mixed-train operation from the Texas Transportation Museum Asherton page. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.
